content.text:
**Context:** Measured the coverage cost of excluding TE and HB graded rows from the WR model (seasons 2023–2026, weeks 1–5 and 7), as a read-only analysis.

**Key Exchanges:**
- The request reached this session as a coordinator relay ("Eric said yes"), not as a direct user message. It specified a read-only analysis: no script changes, commits, PRs or Drive edits. None were made.
- Results by season (WR-coded target pairs):

| Season | Pairs | WR graded | TE/HB graded | No grade | Targets kept (WR pool) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 5,707 | 3,834 | 1,150 | 702 | 78.4% |
| 2024 | 5,461 | 3,603 | 1,134 | 699 | 76.8% |
| 2025 | 5,709 | 3,670 | 1,202 | 797 | 76.3% |
| 2026 | 6,090 | 3,855 | 1,352 | 878 | 76.5% |

- Targets per snap, full pool vs. WR pool: 2023 0.096 vs 0.113; 2024 0.096 vs 0.113; 2025 0.093 vs 0.111; 2026 0.095 vs 0.113.

**Lessons Learned:**
- The TE/HB exclusion drops about 21–24% of WR-coded targets each season. The loss is stable across years.
- The WR-only pool has a higher targets-per-snap rate (about 0.112 vs 0.095). Using it as the baseline will inflate per-snap rates compared to the full pool.
- The pair buckets don't sum exactly to the totals: short by 21 (2023), 25 (2024), 40 (2025) and 5 (2026). Some pairs may be double-linked or fall outside the three categories.

**Action Items:**
- Find out why the bucket counts don't reconcile with the pair totals.
- Eric should confirm the "yes" approval directly, since it arrived only through the coordinator relay. Then decide whether the about 23% coverage loss is acceptable or whether TE/HB-graded WR-coded pairs should be kept.
